name: Theta Ursae Majoris
description: A naked-eye star 13.5 parsecs away, 2.4 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 82328: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.632 +/- 0.005 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 2.365 +/- 0.008

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 82328: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.506 +/- 0.095

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 82328: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6300 +/- 33

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1018776176872261248 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 82328: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 74.18 +/- 0.13 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 13 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 2.4 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.632 milliarcseconds, which gives 2.365 solar radii and 6,300 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 82328: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
